product: VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for Networks
spec_title: VCF Operations for networks API Reference
note: Derived by hand from the OpenAPI document recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Only the two operations this client uses are reproduced here. Property lists are faithful to the spec: every property the spec declares on a request schema is listed, with its spec-declared `required` flag and `default`.

security.note: The spec also declares an unused OpsTokenAuth (http/bearer/JWT) scheme. This client uses ApiKeyAuth. The value prefix is the literal word NetworkInsight followed by a single space and the token; it is not `Bearer`.

ip.spec_description: IP address of data source (use either IP or FQDN, not both)

fqdn.spec_description: Hostname of data source (use either IP or FQDN, not both)

proxy_id.spec_description: ID of Collector VM which should register this vcenter

ipfix_enabled.spec_description: Whether or not to configure vCenter to send IPFIX to Operations for Networks

VCenterDataSourceValidationRequest.note: This schema has no nickname, notes or enabled property. Those exist only on the add-side schema.

VCenterDataSourceRequest.spec_composition: allOf[BaseDataSourceRequest, {credentials, ipfix_request, antrea_ipfix_request, is_vmc, ds_sub_type, tags, enable_ds_associated_tags}]

ip.spec_description: IP address of data source (use either IP or FQDN, not both)

fqdn.spec_description: Hostname of data source (use either IP or FQDN, not both)

proxy_id.spec_description: ID of Collector VM which should register this vcenter

nickname.spec_description: A friendly nickname for the data source

enabled.spec_description: Whether or not data collection is enabled

notes.spec_description: Room for notes or comments about the data source

VCenterDataSourceRequest.note: This schema has no ipfix_enabled property. ipfix_enabled belongs to the validation schema only.

BaseDataSourceValidationResponse.note: Returned with HTTP 200 by validateVCenter. The body-level `code` carries the validation verdict independently of the HTTP status; the spec example for a successful validation is {"code": 200, "message": "Validation successful."}. An HTTP 200 with a body `code` other than 200 is a failed validation, not a success.

VCenterDataSource.spec_composition: allOf[BaseDataSource, {credentials, ipfix_request, antrea_ipfix_request, ipfix_response, antrea_ipfix_response, is_vmc, ds_sub_type, tags, enable_ds_associated_tags}]

entity_id.spec_description: Internal ID of data source, to be used in subsequent API calls

wire_rules: Request bodies are serialized as application/json.

A property the caller has not set is omitted from the JSON object entirely. It is never sent as an empty string, a zero, a false, or a null. This matters most for the spec properties that carry a non-zero default: `enabled` defaults to true on VCenterDataSourceRequest, so sending `"enabled": false` for a caller who never asked to disable collection would silently change behaviour.
`ip` and `fqdn` are mutually exclusive. Exactly one is sent; the other is omitted.
A property that does not exist on the operation's request schema is never sent, even if a similarly named property exists on the other operation's schema.
